answer: An agent registry can require every identity to lock a refundable stake and earn reputation through repeated, randomly assigned trades. At each ledge, a verifier chosen by a lantern protocol challenges the agent with private, task-specific evidence; failed or colluding agents lose collateral and reputation, while honest partners gain access to larger markets. Creating thousands of fake identities therefore requires thousands of deposits and sustained successful behavior, making a Sybil attack expensive before it reaches the summit.
